subject: Per-token ladder: marginal rates, structured credits & fixed-cover breakpoints
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@chatlytic.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for high-volume per-token usage & commit tiers

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — Evan and I walked away excited about Redwood's latency and cost controls. We're doing some internal modeling and need a clearer picture of how you structure per-token volume discounts once we commit to a tier. Two quick questions:  

1) Do you apply discounts on a marginal basis (each breakpoint price applied only to usage within that band) or a blended rate across total usage?
2) For customers who want to keep a tight monthly spend window, do you offer a structured credit / fixed-cover (a small fixed payment that covers a base QPS and then per-token for overages) arrangement? If so, how do you reflect that in the ladder?

We're planning to forecast 10B tokens/month in Q4 with a growth ramp. Attached is our rough expected_usage.csv — would appreciate an example invoice math for both marginal and blended approaches so we can show finance.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
Chatlytic Inc.

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the CSV. Looping in Soojin (pricing) and Marissa (rev ops) so you get the worked math. Quick answer up-front: we support both marginal and blended constructs; many customers prefer marginal for transparency, but blended is available for simplified billing or if you want a single committed effective rate. We also have a structured-credit option that mixes a fixed-monthly cover with a thinner marginal ladder for overages.

I'll let Soojin share a short worked example and attach a draft commit proposal we've used for similar deals.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pricing for high-volume per-token usage & commit tiers

Hi Maya — diving into the numbers you sent. Below are two concise worked examples using a hypothetical ladder; I'll keep the math explicit so finance can reproduce it.

Assumptions (example ladder):
- Breakpoints (monthly committed tokens): 0-1B @ $0.000020/token, 1B-5B @ $0.000018/token, 5B-20B @ $0.000015/token
- Your forecast: 10B tokens for the month

A) Marginal pricing (banded):
- First 1B @ $0.000020 = $20,000
- Next 4B (1B-5B) @ $0.000018 = $72,000
- Remaining 5B (5B-10B) @ $0.000015 = $75,000
- Total = $167,000 -> Effective marginal-weighted average = $0.0000167/token

B) Blended pricing (single effective rate across all usage):
- If we agreed a blended effective rate of $0.000016/token for 10B -> Total = $160,000
- Note: blended gives predictable per-token figure but requires larger commitment or a guaranteed minimum duration to protect Redwood vs bursty demand.

C) Structured-cover (fixed-cover + overage ladder):
- Example: $75k/month fixed cover that 'buys' first 4.5B tokens (effective $0.0000167/token within cover).
- Overages above 4.5B follow a marginal ladder but with slightly higher overage rates to compensate for the lower fixed cover (e.g., overage bands start at $0.0000175 then step down).
- This approach stabilizes spend for you while giving us predictable baseline utilization.

Points to consider:
- Marginal is best for transparency and when usage distribution is stable.
- Blended is helpful for cap/forecasting simplicity but reduces upside if usage is below forecast.
- Structured-credit is our recommended compromise for customers who need a narrower monthly budget window but still want unit economics benefits.

If you want, we can produce a short three-row table (Marginal vs Blended vs Structured-cover) showing monthly totals for Q3/Q4 ramps. Marissa — can you confirm any legal/term constraints around minimum duration vs blended pricing?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Principal Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick CFO notes from rev ops:  
- Blended deals typically require a 12-month minimum or a quarterly true-up clause.
- Structured-cover deals usually include a 6-month commit with a two-quarter review cadence and a standard make-whole clause if growth materially exceeds forecasts.
- We'll also add a one-time implementation credit option for first-month smoothing (applies only to Structured-cover).

Maya — attaching the proposal (commit_proposal_v2.pdf) contains an example SLA kicker for latency-sensitive endpoints. If you'd like, we can run a model that shows blended vs marginal across your Q3 ramp (we'll reuse your CSV).

Best,

Maya — quick follow-up after internal finance sync. A couple of action items: 

1) Finance prefers a blended quote for the first 3 months to simplify vendor approvals, then convert to marginal after a three-month true-up. Can Redwood support an automatic conversion clause?
2) For the structured-cover option, they'd like the fixed cover to be tied to a 90th percentile QPS guarantee on the endpoints that will be most active. Can you confirm Redwood can instrument and report that metric monthly?

If those two things can be confirmed, I think we can move to a cover-letter and legal redline. One small ask: could you provide both the marginal-band math and the single blended-line item as separate line items in the proposal — our procurement team wants it side-by-side.

Thanks all — Evan
Director of Platform Engineering
Chatlytic Inc.
